name: get_positions
description: Track where a satellite is right now (or in the next few seconds): get its live latitude, longitude, altitude, and look-angles (azimuth/elevation) from an observer on Earth. Use this to answer "where is the ISS right now?" (NORAD id 25544) or to locate any satellite by NORAD id. Example: get_positions({ norad_id: 25544, lat: 40.71, lon: -74.0 }).

norad_id.description: NORAD catalog id of the satellite, e.g. 25544 for the ISS, 20580 for Hubble.

altitude.description: Observer altitude in meters above sea level (default 0).

seconds.description: Number of future seconds of positions to predict (default 2, max 300).

_apiKey.description: Optional — your own N2YO API key for higher limits; omit to use the shared Pipeworx key.

name: get_visual_passes
description: Find when a satellite will be visible to the naked eye overhead from an observer location (visual passes = bright, sunlit passes against a dark sky). Returns start/max/end times, elevation, azimuths, brightness magnitude, and duration. Use this for "when can I see the ISS pass over?" Example: get_visual_passes({ norad_id: 25544, lat: 40.71, lon: -74.0 }).

norad_id.description: NORAD catalog id of the satellite, e.g. 25544 for the ISS.

altitude.description: Observer altitude in meters above sea level (default 0).

days.description: Number of days ahead to search for passes (default 5, max 10).

min_visibility.description: Minimum visible duration in seconds for a pass to be returned (default 300).

_apiKey.description: Optional — your own N2YO API key for higher limits; omit to use the shared Pipeworx key.

name: whats_above
description: List what satellites are currently above a location on Earth, within a given radius of the observer's zenith. Use this to answer "what satellites are overhead right now?" Optionally filter by category (e.g. 52 = Starlink, 18 = amateur radio, 1 = brightest). Example: whats_above({ lat: 40.71, lon: -74.0 }).

altitude.description: Observer altitude in meters above sea level (default 0).

radius.description: Search radius in degrees from the observer zenith (default 70, max 90).

category.description: N2YO category filter: 0 = all (default), 18 = amateur radio, 52 = Starlink, 1 = brightest.

_apiKey.description: Optional — your own N2YO API key for higher limits; omit to use the shared Pipeworx key.
